title: Kima's family farm in the hills
body: Kima lives with her family in a small hill village of the north-east. Every few years, the adults of the village choose a patch of forest, cut down the trees and bushes, and burn them. The ash is mixed into the soil, and the family sows rice, maize and vegetables using a hoe and digging sticks. Water reaches the field through a bamboo channel from a spring higher up the slope. They do not buy fertilisers or improved seeds, and almost everything they harvest is eaten by the family. Kima's grandmother says the harvests from a patch are good in the first year or two but grow smaller each season after that.

title: Choosing regions for fibre crops
body: An agricultural officer compares two regions for growing fibre crops. Region X lies in the eastern part of India on the flood plain of a large river. Its soils are fertile and well drained, and fresh silt is laid down on the fields by floods every year. Temperatures stay high through the growing season. Region Y lies in a drier part of the Deccan plateau. Its soil is black and deep. Temperatures are high, rainfall is light, and some fields are irrigated from wells. The region has more than 210 frost-free days in a year and plenty of bright sunshine during the growing season.
